title: Owensboro nurse turns Bigfoot sighting into books, Squatch Fest
excerpt: Sasquatch, Yeti, Bigfoot, Wendigo and Skunk Ape — all different names for the large mythical creature said to lurk in the shadows, staying out of human eyesight (mostly) — and
content:
Sasquatch, Yeti, Bigfoot, Wendigo and Skunk Ape — all different names for the large mythical creature said to lurk in the shadows, staying out of human eyesight (mostly) — and Owensboro's John Reiners, a nurse at Owensboro Health, said that he was skeptical of all of them following a chance encounter in 2020.

"I worked at the hospital, in the COVID unit. I was also working on another unit, and they swabbed me one morning. Long story short, I was on the way into the hospital the next night, and they called and told me that I couldn't come in because I had COVID," said Reiners.

He explained that at the time he and his wife were caring for her elderly father with pre-dementia, so he didn't want to risk getting him sick and decided to quarantine at the family's cabin at Rough River Lake.

"I'm going down (Highway) 54 through Fordsville toward McQuady, and about a mile before McQuady, I see this big deer come across the road, and I see this creature lurking down there," he said. "The deer takes off, and this thing gets up on two feet. I thought, 'COVID's not supposed to make me hallucinate.' I sat there for a long time like petrified."

Before that sighting, Reiners said that he wasn't "into Bigfoot or anything like that."

"So, I wanted answers, and I found out there was no book ever written about anything on 'all fours.' There were certain chapters, but not an entire book," said Reiners.

The revelation led him to pen "Crouching Behemoth: Quadrupedal Sasquatch," which was released on Amazon.com in March 2025.

Amazon describes the book as "the first book of its kind ... the result of an almost three-year deep dive" into research surrounding Bigfoot.

Reiners sat down and interviewed Dr. Jeffrey Meldrum, a former professor of anatomy and anthropology in the Department of Biological Sciences at Idaho State University and an expert in Bigfoot research, as part of "Crouching Behemoth: Quadrupedal Sasquatch."

"He was the foremost primatologist who actually believed in Bigfoot, so I got in touch with him — it took a while," Reiners said. "But when I interviewed him, I told him I had a strong orthopedic background, so I wanted some advice — since he believed in Bigfoot — how would they maneuver on all fours and do all these weird kind of movements. So, we had a long discussion about joints and stuff like that. There are two whole chapters in (the book) all about that."

But Reiners said the most important piece of advice her received from the doctor was to avoid getting on Bigfoot groups and websites online because "all kinds of people come out of the woodwork."

"And I knew that if Dr. Meldrum wanted to be in the book, I had to have flesh and blood, so I started finding podcasts. I went on a podcast or two, and a few of them gave me some names of people that they had talked to and from there, you start finding your network," he said.

After finishing "Crouching Behemoth: Quadrupedal Sasquatch," Reiners said that he enjoyed the process so much that he decided to research another topic surrounding Bigfoot sightings near the local rivers.

"I like to write books that fill a niche that aren't what people normally have. There's a million Bigfoot books of just encounters, but for (the next one) I started thinking about the rivers around here, and I happened to bump into a fisherman who had been at the Green River...who claimed to see the Spotsville Monster. He claimed to see one there, and I thought, 'I bet that they use these waterways to escape and move around.'," he said.

The idea of connecting Bigfoot to the local waterways morphed into Reiners's second book about the mythical creature, called "Aquatic Sasquatch."

He said that he interviewed Native American descendants and "a whole bunch of other people" for the book.

"What they have to say is fascinating," Reiners said. "And I always find, whether somebody believes or not — it's hard to convince people to believe — it's good reading. Each chapter, wherever there is a witness, I highlight the area...Like if it's in a national park, I'll give statistics about the park and fun stuff to see in the area, so there's a lot of fun stuff...I take some fun detours, and there's some humor in there. I always take everything with just a little touch of humor, and make it fun."

Reiners has used his connections and knowledge, alongside event organizer Fred Chisholm, whom Reiners referred to as "a festival visionary," to help put together the Blue Bridge Squatch Fest, a "family-friendly" event bringing vendors, speakers, food trucks, a car show and more. It will be presented from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 26, at Kentucky Soundstage, the former Malco location on Frederica Street.

The Blue Bridge Squatch Fest is described on visitowensboro.com as "browse unique vendors, hear fascinating stories from Bigfoot and paranormal experts, enjoy live music, grab a bite from local food trucks and snap a photo with the festival's very own resident Sasquatch, Sid!"

Reiners added that face painting and a coloring contest will be available for children, along with both a kids' and adult division of a "Bigfoot calling contest."

"It will also be the perfect place to get a book signed," he added, mentioning that he'll have a vendor table set up for selling both works.

The showing of a family-friendly Bigfoot-related movie is also a part of the festival.

"I'm not supposed to say what movie, but it's a family movie. If people think hard enough, they could probably figure out what movie it is," he said. The festival is able to show the movie because organizers aren't charging for admission to the event.

All of the money raised through the festival, Reiners said, is being donated to the SPC Brandon Scott Mullins Memorial Foundation for "veterans programs."

More information about the upcoming festival can be found under the Facebook group The Blue Bridge Squatch Fest.
